title: Rhythm Conductor: Animate a Figure's Dance Routine with BoomBox Energy and Helmet Shield
description: A RiggedFigure stands on a stage between a BoomBox and a DamagedHelmet. The user choreographs a multi-step dance animation by assigning energy pulses from the BoomBox to drive limb movements, while toggling the DamagedHelmet as a shield that conserves total animation energy across channels. Undo/redo lets the user refine the routine, and coupled inputs ensure changing one limb's intensity redistributes energy to others.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load RiggedFigure.glb centered on a circular stage platform, BoomBox.glb to the left scaled up 80x, and DamagedHelmet.glb floating to the right at head height. Add a ground plane, ambient light, two colored spotlights (magenta on BoomBox, cyan on Helmet), and soft shadows. Camera starts at (0,2,5) looking at the figure. Implement these interactions: (1) A bottom HUD panel shows 4 limb channels (LeftArm, RightArm, LeftLeg, RightLeg) each with a slider 0-100. Total energy across all 4 sliders is conserved at 200 — moving one slider auto-redistributes the deficit proportionally among the others. (2) Clicking the BoomBox toggles a pulsing glow animation and doubles the animation speed multiplier for all limbs; clicking again halves it back. (3) Each limb channel drives a sinusoidal rotation on the corresponding bone of the RiggedFigure — amplitude equals slider value mapped to 0-PI/2 radians, frequency tied to a global BPM. (4) Clicking the DamagedHelmet toggles a shield mode: the helmet orbits the figure and all current slider values are frozen until clicked again, with a visible force-field ring. (5) A timeline bar at the top has 6 keyframe slots. Clicking a slot saves the current slider state plus BoomBox and Helmet toggle states as a keyframe. (6) A Play button interpolates between saved keyframes over 2 seconds each using smooth LERP. (7) Undo and Redo buttons revert or reapply the last slider change or keyframe save, maintaining a history stack of at least 10 states. (8) A BPM knob (60-180) controls global animation frequency. All bones animate in the render loop using sin(time * bpm_factor) * amplitude. Display current total energy and BPM on the HUD. Use dat.gui-free pure HTML/CSS controls for the panel.
